editorial.headline: Open Nationally, Blocked in Bali: Forest and Hunting Retail
editorial.standfirst: Specialised retail in forest and hunting products is nationally open to full foreign ownership, but a foreign investor cannot register it in Bali today.
editorial.body:
A foreign investor cannot register this activity in Bali today, even though the national entry is open to full foreign ownership. That contrast is central to understanding the classification. It is specialised retail trade in commodities from forestry and hunting, with deer, kenari nuts and young bamboo shoots (rebung) given as examples. The code is therefore framed by the goods it retails: products associated with the forest and the hunt, sold through a specialised retail activity.

The listed business scales are deliberately broad: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. The record admits the activity at each of those scales, rather than reserving it for only one size of enterprise. That makes the classification relevant both to a smaller registered retail undertaking and to a larger one, provided the registered activity remains the specialised retail trade described in the scope. Scale changes the context in which the Bali risk finding appears, but it does not alter the national openness recorded for the activity.

Nationally, its PMA status is TERBUKA and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. In plain terms, the national record permits PMA registration and allows a foreign stake of up to 100%. Bali is a different result, not a dilution of that national figure. The Bali entry is blocked on risk-class grounds: at scale Besar, OSS risk is recorded as Low or Medium-Low across every scope. Bali’s island-wide, permanent moratorium blocks PMA registration for activities falling within those Low and Medium-Low risk classifications. The block is recorded in connection with the moratorium of May 2026.

For a founder, the decision has to be read in two layers without treating either as an exception to the other. The national layer says specialised retail in these forest and hunting commodities is open and may be wholly foreign owned. The Bali layer says the same activity cannot be registered there as PMA today because of the permanent moratorium and its recorded risk treatment at scale Besar. Neither statement cancels the other. Together, they establish a clear boundary between national foreign-ownership openness and Bali registration availability.
editorial.pullQuote: The national layer says specialised retail in these forest and hunting commodities is open and may be wholly foreign owned.
